body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), determine the smallest deterministic penalty sequence \(\ell_n\ge1\) for which a fully data-driven estimator and confidence interval, not given \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), or \(r_{en}\), attain uniform risk and honest expected length at most \(C\ell_n\rho_n\) over compact ranges of these indices; prove a matching adaptation lower bound for \(\ell_n\).
body.justification: The oracle theorem exposes but does not resolve the practical cost of learning which of the four obstructions is active.
body.gap: MaWang2020RobustIPW has data-driven trimming for an IPW asymptotic criterion, while the supplied theorem assumes known shell and nuisance certificates; no exact adaptation penalty is available.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether the oracle clipping and interval benchmarks can be implemented from validation data without an avoidable logarithmic loss.
